decision: Claude Code 2.1.319 hands Claude a background subagent's final report as <agent-message from="<agent ID>"> with a frame line to Claude and the report indented by two spaces, which fires UserPromptSubmit with just the tags; the transcript adds a lead-in line before them and a warning after, marks the entry meta with origin kind peer, and then records a transcript-only task-notification for the same subagent
why: the chat showed the report as a message from you and counted its turn as yours, so the session went unread and notified, and history dropped it
evidence: a throwaway session through the live hub; 153 agent-message and 15 cross-session-message entries across the transcripts on the VPS

decision: the hub turns each <agent-message> and <cross-session-message> into a peer item, live and in history, without the lead-in, the warning, the frame and the indent, and names a subagent by its agent ID and another session by its from-name
why: what the other Claude wrote is what you need, and the rest is for Claude; a turn can carry several such messages, so each gets its own item
evidence: peer-message, reduce and history tests; live check through a hub restart

decision: the frame and indent come off a subagent's report only, and only when every line after a first bracketed line is indented
why: a message from another session is not framed, and its own first line may start with a bracket

decision: a peer message's turn counts as a task's, and summaries and titles leave peer messages out
why: like a task notification, Claude Code's way to tell you about it is PushNotification, and a report is not something you asked

decision: the app names a subagent's report after the description of the Agent call whose result carries the agent ID, looked up over the whole chat it shows
why: the Agent call gives the ID as a field live and only inside its text in history, and the call can sit in history while the report is live
evidence: PeerMessage tests; live check in the app

decision: a peer message folds into one quiet line like a run of tool calls, a shade stronger, with an arrow for a message coming in, and opens to the message as markdown in a sunk card with a stripe on its left
why: asked for: like tool calls, slightly different; a report is model output like a reply, so it renders as markdown through the same sanitizer
evidence: screenshots at desktop and phone width

decision: the prompt hook's text for a message from another session
why: only the transcript form was seen; the parser takes the tags with and without the lead-in
